storyBeat: Ana and Emir compare football at Bilino Polje with quiet walks by the Una.

grammar.title: Igram and gledam
grammar.explanation: Igram covers I play, and gledam covers I watch. Add fudbal or utakmica to finish the sentence. These two present forms are enough for a stadium chat today.

grammar.title: Često and ponekad
grammar.explanation: Place često or ponekad before the verb to show how often you do something. Često means often, and ponekad means sometimes. Keep the rest of the sentence in the present.

examples.english: I often go for a walk.

grammar.title: Hobby lines with volim
grammar.explanation: Reuse Volim plus an activity noun or verb. Pair sports with river walks so hobbies feel wider than just one stadium. Short present-tense lines keep the chat friendly.

culture.title: Stadium noise and river calm
culture.body: Zenica's Bilino Polje stadium gives football a loud local home on match days. Ana and Emir talk about the tim, the utakmica, and who watches versus who plays. A second postcard shows Štrbački buk on the Una River, where the water crashes white over stone. Weekend life can mean a packed stand one afternoon and a quiet river walk the next morning. Crowds chant one day, and the path grows still beside the water the next. Hobby words should cover both the stadium noise and the calm walk.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A. Play, watch, and how often
lessonBlocks.body: Begin with sport, hobi, fudbal, utakmica, and tim so the stadium vocabulary feels concrete. Then practice Igram and Gledam as separate present-tense lines you can finish with a noun. Ana often watches, and Emir sometimes plays. The words često and ponekad make that difference clear. Say each sentence while pointing to the Bilino Polje image so the place anchors the verb. Reuse these lines until they feel automatic, no full verb table needed yet. Finish Lesson A by telling a partner how often you watch and how often you play, in two short lines that use both frequency words.
tips: Keep igram and gledam as separate ready lines.
Put često or ponekad before the verb.
Name the team or match to finish the line.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B. From stands to river path
lessonBlocks.body: Move from the stadium to the river postcard without dropping the football words you just learned. Use Volim šetnju and Rijeka Una je lijepa to balance match talk with some outdoor calm. Ask a friend Hoćeš li gledati utakmicu? And answer with često or ponekad plus a present-tense verb. Amira prefers the waterfall walk, while Mrvica prefers any path that might hide snacks. Close by naming one sport habit and one nature habit, both in the present tense. You're describing your own weekend, not reciting a list of abstract hobby nouns. Say your two habits a few times until they sound natural.
tips: Balance football lines with šetnja vocabulary.
Ask Hoćeš li gledati utakmicu? In a friendly voice.
Claim one hobby you will actually repeat.

funFacts.title: Bilino Polje anchors Zenica football
funFacts.body: Bilino Polje is the main football stadium in Zenica. National and club matches have made the ground familiar across the country. The wide stands give you a clear sports image beyond Sarajevo. Saying utakmica beside this ground makes the word feel loud and real.

funFacts.title: Štrbački buk shows the Una
funFacts.body: Štrbački buk is a waterfall stretch on the Una River near the northwestern border area. White water over wide stone shelves draws walkers and photographers. This postcard balances the stadium noise with river calm, because hobby vocabulary needs both kinds of weekend.

funFacts.title: Često beats a long verb table
funFacts.body: Frequency adverbs let beginners talk about habits truthfully without learning new tenses. Često and ponekad fit right in front of present verbs you already know. The pattern is small and reusable, and being honest about how often you play keeps the conversation human.

funFacts.title: Hobi can be quiet
funFacts.body: Not every hobby is a competitive sport. Šetnja along a river counts, and so does watching from the stands. Book 1 keeps the word open on purpose. Pick the activity you'll actually repeat.

civicContext.title: Cantons and private colleges fracture higher education
civicContext.body: Weekend sport talk sits next to a struggling education system for young adults. In the Federation, cantons fund and oversee public universities, while Republika Srpska runs a separate system. Dozens of private colleges opened after 2000, and quality varies sharply between them. Weak oversight has let some private schools sell credentials rather than real training. Which canton or entity stamps a diploma can matter almost as much as the skill behind it.
